question.text: Under SEBI AIF Regulations, side pocket (segregated portfolio) treatment is:

answer.text: Mandatory for all Cat I and Cat II AIFs.
Permitted only for Cat III AIFs; NOT typical for Cat I/II.

explanation.text: The Logic: Side pockets are a mechanism to segregate illiquid / distressed assets from the main portfolio - they are primarily relevant for open-ended Cat III schemes to protect exiting investors. Cat I/II are close-ended with fixed LP commitments, so side-pockets are not typical. The Trap: 'Mandatory Cat I/II' overstates. 'Angel only' is fabricated. 'Automatic for debt' confuses with Cat III debt funds. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-E (future Cat III exam) will test side pockets in depth. XIX-D treats them as cross-ref only. Manager's Pro-Tip: For Cat I/II, use 'liquidation account' or 'retained distributions' mechanics instead of side-pockets to handle illiquid tail-end holdings - side-pocket language is for Cat III.
